extracted.intended_audience: natural gas pipeline companies, public utilities, applicants, intervenors, and counsel participating in Federal Power Commission (FPC) / Natural Gas Act proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing filings, notices, interventions, suspensions, hearings, and amendments in Federal Power Commission dockets under the Natural Gas Act (rate filings, certificate applications, petitions to amend, and related matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing of notices of intervention / petitions to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of intervention or petitions to intervene may be filed with the Federal Power Commission, Washington, D.C. 20426, in accordance with the rules of practice and procedure (e.g., 18 CFR 1.8, 1.10, and 1.37(f)) on or before the date specified in the notice (various dates given, e.g., February 15, 1968; January 22, 1968; January 29, 1968).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited rules of practice and procedure (18 CFR 1.8, 1.10, 1.37(f)) and meet the specific deadline stated in the notice for that docket. The notice typically provides the Commission address and the exact last date for filing; failure to file by that date may preclude intervention. Petitions/protests should state grounds and comply with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and public inspection of applications and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, amendments, and petitions filed in Commission dockets are 'on file with the Commission and open to public inspection.' Notices specify the nature of the filing and the location for inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure filings include sufficient descriptive material so the public and interested parties can inspect the application on file. Expect that protests or petitions to intervene will reference the public filing; provide complete documents for the Commission record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission authority to suspend proposed rate changes pending hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Natural Gas Act (sections 4 and 15) and the Commission's rules, proposed supplements or rate schedules may be suspended and their use deferred pending a public hearing and decision when questions arise as to lawfulness or where the proposed rate 'may be unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, or preferential, or otherwise unlawful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may order suspension for specified periods (examples in the text include 1 day or 5 months) when a proposed rate exceeds applicable area ceilings or raises other legal concerns. Filers should anticipate suspension if proposed rates exceed established ceilings or otherwise implicate statutory standards; refunds and interest may be addressed where temporary conditioned rates were in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area ceiling and initial service ceiling limits as a check on proposed rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed increased rates are measured against 'applicable area increased rate ceiling' and 'initial service ceiling' (examples: 11 cents per Mcf ceiling; 17 cents initial service ceiling; specific area ceilings such as 16.39 cents per Mcf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposed rate exceeds the area's established ceiling, the Commission is likely to suspend the filing and may ultimately reject the increase. Filers should determine applicable area ceilings (including any adjustments like treating costs) before proposing increases, and justify why an exception should be made if the proposed rate exceeds the ceiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of conditions in temporary certificates (Condition (2) precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition (2) in temporary certificates (stating that the conditioned rate shall remain in effect until changed by Commission order) may be waived by the Commission in the public interest. In similar cases the Commission has waived Condition (2) for other producers after expiration of a 3-year period between date of initial delivery and request for a rate increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where deliveries under a temporary certificate began more than three years before a rate increase request, the Commission has precedent to waive Condition (2) to permit filing of a notice of change. Applicants seeking waiver should cite the public interest and comparable precedent; expect the Commission to analyze the length of service and other equities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds triggering public hearing on rate lawfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission finds it 'necessary and proper in the public interest and to aid in the enforcement of the provisions of the Natural Gas Act' to enter a public hearing concerning the lawfulness of proposed increases when the proposed change raises questions (e.g., exceeds ceilings or may be unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, preferential, or otherwise unlawful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public hearing will be set by notice from the Secretary; parties should prepare to support the lawfulness of a proposed rate or to challenge it on statutory/record grounds. The Commission will defer use of the proposed rate pending hearing and decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no protest filed, Commission may grant certificate after internal review without further notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no protest or petition to intervene is filed within the time required, the Commission may on its own review find that a grant of the certificate (or other relief) is required by the public convenience and necessity and will hold a hearing 'without further notice' before the Commission (i.e., no additional public procedural notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that absence of protests can streamline the process; however, the Commission still may conduct an internal review before grant. Even if no hearing occurs, the applicant should ensure the record demonstrates that the grant is required by public convenience and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rule for competitive applications (18 CFR §157.11(a) standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a competitive application 'is filed less than 15 days prior to the commencement of a hearing' the Commission 'will not schedule the new application for hearing until it has rendered its final decision on such pending application,' except when it finds that the public interest requires otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive applicants filing shortly before a scheduled hearing risk having their application deferred until the Commission decides the pending case, unless they can show the public interest requires immediate consideration. Parties opposing consolidation or joinder may raise untimeliness under §157.11(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications to issue securities under the Federal Power Act (section 204) — public notice and competitive bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications under section 204 to issue bonds and additional common stock are noticed; securities are to be sold at competitive bidding pursuant to the Commission's regulations, with proposed invitation-to-bid dates and descriptions of intended uses of proceeds disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose the proposed amount, intended use of proceeds, and proposed sale method (competitive bidding). Interested persons may file protests/petitions to be heard (deadlines provided). Ensure compliance with Commission regulations governing securities issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to prior orders / petitions to amend orders must be filed and are subject to protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to amend prior Commission orders (e.g., to extend a 3‑year authorization period, to construct and operate taps and metering facilities, or to increase volumetric service limits) are filed in the relevant docket, placed on public file, and subject to protests or petitions to intervene by specified dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking amendments (extensions, increased limits, new facilities) provide factual justification (e.g., need for additional gas, changed circumstances), cost estimates, and financing plans; anticipate protests and the possibility of hearings. File within the statutory/regulatory windows stated in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeze on changes to supplements or rate schedules during suspension/pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Until otherwise ordered by the Commission, neither supplements nor the rate schedules sought to be altered shall be changed until disposition of these proceedings or expiration of the suspension period; the supplement 'is hereby suspended and the use thereof deferred' pending hearing and decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a supplement or rate schedule is suspended, parties may not implement the proposed change until the Commission lifts the suspension or issues a final order. Filers should plan for delays and potential refunds if collections were made subject to later findings.
